laws.rule: The legal age for cannabis in Saskatchewan is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from private licensed stores, in person and online.

Cannabis Control (Saskatchewan) Act, S.S. 2018, c. C-2.111: nobody older than a minor (a minor is under 19) may consume cannabis in a public place or any place other than a private place (s. 2-14). The Act's meaning of public place includes parks, playgrounds, roads and streets, and vehicles in those places. Consuming at a school, its grounds or a child care facility is banned (s. 2-16). Nobody may possess, consume or distribute cannabis in a vehicle, except to carry it from where it was lawfully obtained to a place where it may lawfully be had or used (s. 2-10). The minister may ban possessing or consuming cannabis in a provincial park or regional park campground by order (s. 2-17); check for a current order.

Under the same Act, nobody older than a minor may possess more than 30 g of dried cannabis (or its equivalent under Schedule 3) in a public place, or more than 4 non-flowering plants (s. 2-8). Buying cannabis from anyone not authorised to sell it is banned (s. 2-7).

Alcohol and Gaming Regulation Act, 1997, S.S. 1997, c. A-18.011, s. 107: nobody may have, drink or give alcohol in a public place or anywhere other than a private place or permitted premises, unless the Act or regulations allow it. Municipal councils, regional park authorities and some other bodies may designate outdoor public places by bylaw where alcohol may be drunk (s. 107(4)), so rules differ by town and park.

The legal drinking age in Saskatchewan is 19 (minor means under 19, per the Act definition). Selling or giving alcohol to a minor is banned, except that a parent, guardian or spouse may give it in a private place to their child, ward or spouse (s. 110).

Nobody may have, keep, drink or give alcohol in a vehicle, except to carry it from where it was lawfully obtained to a place where it may be lawfully had or drunk, or in a vehicle with a special use permit (s. 109(1) and (2)). The maximum penalty is a C$2,000 fine (about A$2,033 at A$1 = C$0.9838, RBA 30 Oct 2026), two months in jail, or both (s. 109(4)).

items.text: The legal age to buy and use cannabis is 19, the same as alcohol. Adults may carry up to 30 g in public. Cannabis is sold through private stores regulated by the Saskatchewan Liquor and Gaming Authority (SLGA).

Using cannabis in public places is banned, and so is using it in a vehicle, as driver or passenger. Set fines include C$200 (about A$203) for using it in a public place or carrying more than 30 g in public, C$300 (about A$305) for possessing or using it in a vehicle, and C$1,000 (about A$1,016) for using it at a school or child care facility, at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = CAD 0.9838.

The legal drinking age is 19. Since 23 May 2023 municipalities and park authorities can pass a bylaw designating outdoor public places, such as parks, where adults may drink; the areas and hours must be posted, and provincial liquor rules still apply there.
